issue.title: actstat and bob-cli committed a half-updated feature task-type snapshot: agent_creatable is right but create_refusal is the retired machine-policy copy
issue.description:
Proposed by sase-tn.land while landing epic sase-tn (plans:202608/feature_task_type_default.md).
The epic's own plan named this in its "After the epic lands" section (D4) and deliberately
scoped it out of every phase, because the regeneration must run against an installed `sase`
that already carries the epic's commit.

ROOT CAUSE (verified, not inferred): epic sase-tn landed in two commits with different
effects on other projects' committed task-type snapshots.

- Phase sase-tn.1 removed the machine-global `bead.task_types` disable from
  `~/.config/sase/sase.yml` (chezmoi), which made `builtin@feature` agent-creatable
  everywhere. That effect went live via chezmoi's `commit_hooks.after` at ~12:59.
- Phase sase-tn.2 (5ca05f6a5, 13:01) replaced the builtin `create_refusal` copy in
  `src/sase/task_types/_builtin.py`, changing the `feature` spec digest from
  9445f9171caf31b5 to c461e1e8c92d50f2.

Both actstat and bob-cli were regenerated at 13:02 by `chore: run sase init memory`
(actstat 9b04411, bob-cli 5c01b3f), one minute after 5ca05f6a5. That run picked up phase 1
but not phase 2, because the uv-tool editable checkout backing `/home/bryan/.local/bin/sase`
had not pulled 5ca05f6a5 yet. Both repos therefore committed the half-updated state.

CURRENT STATE (both repos, sase/task_types.json `feature` entry):
  agent_creatable: true, source: builtin, package: sase   <- correct (phase 1)
  digest: 9445f9171caf31b5                                <- stale (pre-phase-2)
  create_refusal: "... That is the machine-global override outside the SASE project.
                   File a feature bead only in SASE, or use an in-scope type here."

So Symptom 2 from the epic's plan -- a shipped default that names one machine's policy
and one user's project -- is still committed in two projects even though it is gone from
sase itself. `sase/memory/task_types/feature.md` and the `sase/memory/task_types.md`
roster in both repos are keyed to that stale digest.

The installed `sase` is now current: `sase bead task-type show feature --json` from
/home/bryan/.local/bin/sase reports digest c461e1e8c92d50f2 and the new copy, so the D4
ordering precondition is satisfied and the fix is unblocked.

WHY THIS IS NOT DONE ALREADY: `sase memory init` in those repos rewrites files under
`sase/memory/`, and an agent may not modify memory files on an agent-produced plan's
authorization alone. This needs the project owner's go-ahead in the turn that runs it.

FIX (one command per repo, from each project's checkout):
  sase repo open actstat -r "Regenerate the task-type snapshot after sase-tn"
  cd <printed path> && sase memory init
  sase repo open bob-cli  -r "Regenerate the task-type snapshot after sase-tn"
  cd <printed path> && sase memory init

Expect exactly one changed area per repo: the `feature` entry in sase/task_types.json
moves to digest c461e1e8c92d50f2 with the new create_refusal, and the feature strand /
roster refresh alongside it. `agent_creatable`, `source`, and `package` should not move.

VERIFICATION: `sase validate` in each repo currently reports the drift and names
`sase memory init` as the fix, so nothing fails silently while this is open.

task_type_fields.proposed_change:
Run `sase memory init` in the actstat and bob-cli checkouts so their
`sase/memory/task_types/feature.md` strand, `sase/memory/task_types.md` roster, and
`sase/task_types.json` snapshot carry the policy-neutral `create_refusal` copy and digest
c461e1e8c92d50f2 that epic sase-tn shipped, instead of the retired copy that names one
machine's config layer and tells agents to "File a feature bead only in SASE".
